question: For a short electric dipole, use the expression for potential at a point to discuss its dependence on distance and angle. A dipole has dipole moment $p = 3 \times 10^{-8}\text{ C m}$. Calculate the potential at a point $0.30\text{ m}$ from its centre when the point makes an angle $60^\circ$ with the dipole moment. Take $\frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} = 9 \times 10^9\text{ N m}^2\text{ C}^{-2}$.

options.D: $V=\frac{kp\cos\theta}{r^2}$, so $V\propto\frac{1}{r^2}$ and depends on $\cos\theta$; at $r=0.30\,\text{m}$ and $\theta=60^\circ$, $V=1.5\times10^3\,\text{V}$
